articles.title: Critical Alert SMS API Economics: Polling Evidence Before Retry and Resend
articles.excerpt: For a marketplace sending new-order SMS notifications to sellers, the dominant variable is often not the send itself. It is everything retained and repeatedly read afterward: status polls, event recor…
articles.body: For a marketplace sending new-order SMS notifications to sellers, the dominant variable is often not the send itself. It is everything retained and repeatedly read afterward: status polls, event records, retry attempts, and audit data. TL;DR: choose an SMS API only after calculating that observation load. A polling API is a sound fit for critical outage alerts when your backend can schedule delivery-status checks, stop them at a deadline, and own retry, escalation, cancellation, and country controls. If a seller must trigger an immediate multistep escalation from a delivery event, a push-oriented product deserves more weight. The useful change is to poll according to the remaining value of the notification, not forever at one fixed interval.

articles.title: Database Indexing – Part 1: How Indexes Help Find Data Faster
articles.excerpt: Recently, I was reading two books: Good Vibes, Good Life and The Mountain Is You. I usually forget things after some time 😅. So whenever I want to revisit something I've read, I go back to the book.…
articles.body: Recently, I was reading two books: Good Vibes, Good Life and The Mountain Is You . I usually forget things after some time 😅. So whenever I want to revisit something I've read, I go back to the book. But I noticed one difference between these two books. Good Vibes, Good Life has an index at the end of the book. Whenever I want to read about a particular topic, I can look at the index, find the page number, and directly go to that page. But The Mountain Is You doesn't have that kind of index. So if I remember a topic but don't remember where I read it, I have to go through the chapters one by one until I find it. That takes more time, right? The same thing happens in databases. Imagine we have a table containing millions of records, and we want to find one particular record.

articles.title: I almost rebuilt a project for the wrong reason, a 20 minute audit caught it
articles.excerpt: I have an iPhone-driving rig. An ESP32 board plugs into the phone over USB and plays human, screen taps, button presses, the works, so my local agent can actually operate the phone instead of just tal…
articles.body: I have an iPhone-driving rig. An ESP32 board plugs into the phone over USB and plays human, screen taps, button presses, the works, so my local agent can actually operate the phone instead of just talking about it. The rig works. It has worked for months. So naturally my first instinct was to rebuild the whole thing from scratch. The reason I gave myself was security. The codebase came from a mixed-background project, there were Chinese translation files in the repo, a bundled JavaScript front end I had never actually read, and firmware binaries I had flashed without ever opening in a hex editor. In my head the story was already written: old rig is sketchy, new rig is clean, rebuild obviously justified. Before I burned a month on it I made myself audit the old code first.

articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
